mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 6 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for 6 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 5-year rolling windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases equity discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS has exceeded 5.0% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in private sector employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls simultaneously, or the Rank IC for the joint signal is below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) combined with high consumer credit (RSAFS) indicates weakening demand for housing and durable goods, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods when HOUST declines and RSAFS is high, or the Rank IC for the joint signal in late-cycle is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past 3 months indicates robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where INDPRO has increased for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 4-year rolling windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1,400,000 units for two consecutive months, it signals strong consumer demand for housing, boosting retail and construction sectors and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where HOUST exceeds 1400.0 for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high labor market slack (UNRATE > 4.5%), a decline in private sector employment (PAYEMS) indicates deteriorating economic conditions that reduce corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE > 4.5% and PAYEMS declines, or the Rank IC for the PAYEMS signal in high unemployment slack regimes is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100.0 for two consecutive months, it signals a contraction in manufacturing output that reduces corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where INDPRO falls below 100.0 for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 2-year rolling windows is below 0.02.
